questions.text: What is the maximum period for which a bank can hold a 'Doubtful Asset' before it is classified as a 'Loss Asset' if it remains uncollectible?

options.text: There is no fixed period; it depends on the auditor/RBI inspection
None of the Above

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is There is no fixed period; it depends on the auditor/RBI inspection.

Key Points

  • According to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) guidelines, a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) is classified into three categories based on the period for which the asset has remained non-performing: Sub-standard, Doubtful, and Loss Assets.
  • A Sub-standard Asset is one that has remained an NPA for a period less than or equal to 12 months. If an asset stays in the sub-standard category for more than 12 months, it is subsequently classified as a Doubtful Asset.
  • A Loss Asset is defined as an asset where loss has been identified by the bank, its internal or external auditors, or during an RBI inspection, but the amount has not been written off wholly.
  • Crucially, there is no fixed time-bound transition from the Doubtful category to the Loss category. An asset remains "Doubtful" until it is specifically identified as "uncollectible" by an authority. Hence, Option D is the correct statement.
  • Options 1 Year, 2 Years, and 3 Years are incorrect because while they relate to sub-categories of doubtful assets (D1, D2, D3), they do not trigger an automatic classification as a Loss Asset. Hence, statements A, B, and C are incorrect.

Additional Information

  • Categories of Doubtful Assets: To refine risk assessment, Doubtful Assets are divided into three tiers based on the duration they have spent in the doubtful category:
    • Doubtful 1 (D1): Up to one year.
    • Doubtful 2 (D2): Between one and three years.
    • Doubtful 3 (D3): More than three years.
  • Provisioning Norms: Banks are required to hold a certain percentage of the loan value as a "provision." For the secured portion of Doubtful Assets, the requirements are 25% for D1, 40% for D2, and 100% for D3. For any unsecured portion, a 100% provisioning is mandatory regardless of the category.
  • Identification of Loss Assets: Because Loss Assets are considered uncollectible and have little to no value as a bankable asset, they require 100% provisioning immediately upon identification. These assets are typically written off the books to clean the balance sheet, though recovery efforts may continue.
  • Special Mention Accounts (SMA): Before an account becomes an NPA (overdue for 90 days), it is classified as SMA to alert the bank of potential stress. SMA-0 covers 1-30 days, SMA-1 covers 31-60 days, and SMA-2 covers 61-90 days.

Important Points

  • The primary regulation governing these classifications in India is the RBI Master Circular on Prudential Norms on Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning (IRAC).
  • The role of the Statutory Auditor is vital in this process. During the annual audit, if the auditor finds that the collateral value of a Doubtful Asset has eroded significantly (less than 10% of the outstanding), the asset can be directly classified as a Loss Asset without waiting for further time to pass.
  • The Banking Regulation Act, 1949 empowers the RBI to inspect banks and ensure that these classifications are strictly followed to maintain the financial stability of the economy.

questions.text: What is the current ceiling for a single loan under the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) in the 'Tarun' category?

options.text: None of the Above

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Rs. 10 Lakhs.

Key Points

  • The Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) is a flagship scheme launched by the Government of India on April 8, 2015, to provide collateral-free loans up to Rs. 10 Lakhs to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro-enterprises.
  • The 'Tarun' category is the third and highest tier under the standard PMMY framework, specifically designed for micro-units that have reached a stage of growth and require higher funding for diversification or expansion.
  • The loan amount under the Tarun category ranges from above Rs. 5,00,000 to Rs. 10,00,000. This ensures that maturing small businesses have access to the capital required for significant upgrades. Hence, the statement regarding the Rs. 10 Lakhs ceiling for the Tarun category is correct.
  • MUDRA loans are refinanced by the Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA), which is a subsidiary of SIDBI (Small Industries Development Bank of India).
  • The scheme aims to "fund the unfunded" by bringing small entrepreneurs into the formal financial system, reducing their reliance on informal moneylenders.

Additional Information

  • Categorization of PMMY Loans:
    • Shishu: This stage covers loans up to Rs. 50,000. It is primarily targeted at startups and entrepreneurs in the initial stage of their business journey.
    • Kishore: This stage covers loans above Rs. 50,000 and up to Rs. 5,00,000. It is intended for units that are already operational and require funds for purchase of equipment or working capital.
    • Tarun: As discussed, it covers loans up to Rs. 10,00,000 for expansion purposes.
  • Recent Budgetary Update (2024): In the Union Budget 2024-25, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman announced that the limit for MUDRA loans will be enhanced to Rs. 20 Lakhs under a new 'Tarun Plus' category for those entrepreneurs who have successfully repaid their previous loans under the Tarun category.
  • Eligible Borrowers: Individuals, Proprietorship firms, Partnership firms, Small Manufacturing units, Service sector units, Shopkeepers, Fruit and Vegetable vendors, and Artisans are eligible to apply.
  • Lending Institutions: These loans can be availed from Commercial Banks, Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), Small Finance Banks, MFIs (Micro Finance Institutions), and NBFCs (Non-Banking Financial Companies).

Important Points

  • MUDRA Card: Borrowers are provided with a MUDRA Card, which is a RuPay Debit Card. This card allows the borrower to withdraw the working capital portion of the loan in multiple installments as per the requirement of the business.
  • Credit Guarantee: Loans under PMMY are covered under the Credit Guarantee Fund for Micro Units (CGFMU), which is managed by the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC). This removes the need for third-party collateral.
  • Processing Fees: Generally, banks do not charge any processing fees for loans under the Shishu category, while a nominal fee may be applicable for Kishore and Tarun categories.
  • Repayment Period: The repayment period for MUDRA loans is usually flexible, ranging from 3 to 5 years, depending on the cash flow of the business and the discretion of the lending bank.
  • Sectors Covered: The scheme covers activities in Land Transport, Community/Social/Personal Service, Food Product Sector, and Textile Product Sector, excluding activities related to core agriculture (though allied activities like poultry and dairy are covered).

questions.text: What is the estimated fiscal deficit for the Union Budget 2026–27 as a percentage of GDP?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 4.3 percent of GDP.

In News

  • The Union Budget 2026-27 estimates the fiscal deficit at 4.3 percent of GDP.

Key Points

  • The fiscal deficit for BE 2026-27 is projected at 4.3 percent of GDP, indicating continued fiscal consolidation.
  • This estimate reflects the gap between total government expenditure of ₹53.5 lakh crore and total receipts excluding borrowings.

Additional Information

  • Fiscal Deficit
    • Fiscal deficit represents the excess of total government expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings.
    • It indicates the amount the government needs to borrow to meet its expenses.
    • Fiscal deficit is commonly expressed as a percentage of GDP to assess sustainability.
  • Budget Estimates (BE)
    • Budget Estimates are the government’s projections of revenue and expenditure for the upcoming financial year.
    • They are presented in the Union Budget before the start of the financial year.
  • Revised Estimates (RE)
    • Revised Estimates update earlier budget projections based on actual spending and receipts during the year.
    • They provide a more realistic picture of fiscal performance.
  • Debt-to-GDP Ratio
    • This ratio measures the government’s total debt in relation to the country’s GDP.
    • A declining ratio indicates improving fiscal health and sustainability.

questions.text: As per the SARFAESI Act 2002, what is the minimum amount of default required to initiate recovery proceedings?

options.text: None of the Above

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Rs. 1 Lakh.

Key Points

  • The SARFAESI Act, 2002 (Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act) provides a legal framework for banks and financial institutions to recover their Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) efficiently.
  • As per Section 31(j) of the SARFAESI Act, 2002, the provisions of the Act shall not apply to any case in which the amount due is less than Rs. 1 Lakh.
  • This minimum threshold of Rs. 1 Lakh is mandatory to ensure that recovery proceedings are initiated for significant defaults and not for trivial amounts.
  • Furthermore, the Act cannot be invoked if the balance amount due is less than 20% of the principal amount and interest thereon.
  • Once an account is classified as an NPA, the secured creditor (the bank) must issue a demand notice under Section 13(2), providing the borrower a period of 60 days to settle the dues before taking possession of the collateral.

Additional Information

  • Non-Performing Asset (NPA): In the context of Indian banking, an asset is classified as an NPA when the interest or principal installment remains overdue for more than 90 days.
  • Exclusions from the Act: Apart from defaults below Rs. 1 Lakh, the SARFAESI Act is strictly not applicable to agricultural land, any security interest created in any vessel or aircraft, and any conditional sale or hire-purchase where no security interest is created.
  • Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs): The Act allows for the establishment of ARCs, which are specialized financial institutions that buy bad loans (NPAs) from banks to clean up their balance sheets and handle the recovery process independently.
  • Debt Recovery Tribunal (DRT): Borrowers who feel aggrieved by the actions of a bank under the SARFAESI Act have the right to file an application for redressal before the DRT within 45 days of the bank taking measures to recover the asset.
  • Objectives: The primary objective of the SARFAESI Act, 2002 is to enable banks to take possession of securities and sell them to recover debt without the time-consuming intervention of courts.

Important Points

  • The SARFAESI Act was formulated based on the recommendations of the Narasimham Committee I and II and the Andhyarujina Committee to reform the financial system and expedite loan recovery.
  • The Act provides three main methods for NPA recovery: Securitisation, Asset Reconstruction, and Enforcement of Security without the interruption of a Civil Court.
  • In 2020, the Supreme Court of India passed a landmark judgment stating that Co-operative Banks can also make use of the SARFAESI Act, 2002 for the recovery of dues from defaulting borrowers.
  • The authorized officer of the secured creditor is responsible for delivering the possession notice and ensuring the valuation of the secured asset before auctioning it in the public market.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a function of money?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Barter system

Key Points

  • Barter system is not a function of money.
  • Money serves as a store of value, enabling individuals to save and defer consumption until a later date.
  • It acts as a unit of account, providing a common measure of the value of goods and services.
  • Money functions as a medium of exchange, facilitating transactions between buyers and sellers.
  • The barter system involves the direct exchange of goods and services without the use of money, which is different from the functions of money.

Additional Information

  • The barter system was prevalent before the invention of money.
  • While the barter system can work in small economies, it is inefficient in larger economies due to the double coincidence of wants problem, where two parties each possess an item the other wants.
  • Money helps to overcome the limitations of the barter system by providing a common medium of exchange.
  • By serving as a store of value, unit of account, and medium of exchange, money simplifies and enhances economic transactions.
  • Modern economies rely on money to facilitate trade, savings, and economic calculation.

more than one acre and up to two acre

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is more than one hectare and up to two hectares.

For the purpose of computation of 8 percent target, Small and Marginal Farmers will include the following:-

  • Farmers with landholding of up to 1 hectare are considered Marginal Farmers. Farmers with a landholding of more than 1 hectare and up to 2 hectares are considered Small Farmers.
  • Landless agricultural labourers, tenant farmers, oral lessees, and share-croppers.
  • Loans to Self Help Groups (SHGs) or Joint Liability Groups (JLGs), i.e. groups of individual Small and Marginal farmers directly engaged in Agriculture and Allied Activities, provided banks maintain disaggregated data of such loans.
  • Loans to farmers' producer companies of individual farmers, and co-operatives of farmers directly engaged in Agriculture and Allied Activities, where the membership of Small and Marginal Farmers is not less than 75 percent by number and whose land-holding share is also not less than 75 percent of the total land-holding.
